name: Hag
body:
Many types of hags walk the world, but those freshly risen from rituals share some common features. They remain close to their humanoid past, only growing monstrous as they develop further.

These hags appear as ancient humanoid women with wrinkled faces and talon-like fingernails. Hags risen from changelings generally appear roughly human, but those rare hags from other races will carry some marks of their past (be that subtly pointed ears or hairy toes).

Although lone hags can be found on the fringes of humanoid society, hags’ own society centers around the coven. These groups gather to perform ritual magic and, although hags are generally loathe to admit it, companionship. Newly transformed changelings are generally brought into the coven that completed their transformation, but non-changelings who have transformed themselves are often left alone.

Few hags survive in the long term without a coven. They search for other hags, even monstrous ones, or reach out to those witches capable of fueling a coven’s magic. The craftiest hags train outsiders in their ways, forming a coven among humanoid outcasts or even adventuring parties.

Beyond the coven, many hags feel some vague allegiance to their “family,” the line of hags stretching mother to mother back into the mists of time. These terms slip into hag speech even among outsiders, referring to respected elders as “aunt” and reserving “grandmother” for the highest of praise.

At the edges of humanoid society, hags can easily be mistaken for witches, alchemists, healers, hedge mages, or wise elders. Many hags live for decades or centuries without transforming into their monstrous counterparts, leaving outsiders to wonder what triggers the final transformation.

Even hags are a little unclear on the point. Powerful hags can draw on the strength of their families, growing even stronger than their monstrous counterparts, but hags who abandon their humanoid roots and shun mortal society transform long before others. Among those hags who don’t wish to transform, living among humanoids can stave off the transformation for decades or even centuries.

Covens

Central to hags’ power and culture, covens are gatherings of magic users who increase their power through dark rituals. Characters can gain the ability to join a coven in multiple ways: the witch’s coven hex, the Coven Training feat below, or class abilities from other sources. Paragon hags in particular can allow a limited number of non-hags into their covens. Covens must consist of at least three members but can contain up to thirteen.

The powers granted by a coven depend on its members. Covens containing monstrous hags gain the benefits listed in the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Bestiary. Covens containing newly transformed hags or paragon hags (see below for both) gain the benefits listed in that race and class. Coven feats also grant the coven new abilities.

Due to the commitment involved, no creature can be a member of more than one coven at a time. Joining a coven requires a nightlong ritual of at least one coven member which is automatically successful. Leaving a coven, on the other hand, is a free action. If a coven falls below three members, it is automatically disbanded.

Traits
Ability Score Modifiers: Hags have shocking force of personality and powerful frames despite their apparent age. They gain +2 Strength and +2 Charisma.
Size: Medium. Hags are medium-sized creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Type: Monstrous Humanoid. Hags are monstrous humanoids rather than normal humanoids and cannot be affected by spells like charm person or enlarge person.
Senses: Darkvision. Hags can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.
Canny: Hags receive a +2 racial bonus to Perception and Sense Motive checks.
Coven Training: Hags gain Coven Training as a bonus feat, allowing them to join or form covens (see Covens above).
Immortal: Though hags continue to hunch and wrinkle as time goes on, they cannot die of old age.
Languages: Hags begin play speaking Common and Giant. Hags with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following for their bonus languages: Abyssal, Aklo, Celestial, Goblin, Infernal, Necril, Orc, and Sylvan.
